messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: SLO ALERT — Dedicated pool 'eu-prod-2' p99 streaming latency breached 30s for the last 3m. p95 ~ 1.8s, p99 ~ 34s. Queue depth rising. Affected routes: /v1/stream/chat (high qps customers). Thresholds: p95>1s, p99>5s. Auto-escalate to #incidents and @oncall.
Nora (oncall): I'm on it. Paging infra and runtime. Any initial customer-visible reports?
Blake (support): Seeing multiple customer timeouts and stalls, e.g. AcmeApp got repeated streaming stalls and a 504. Customer reported degraded UX around 10:18 UTC. They're on Dedicated EU cluster.
Tara (cust-success): Reached out to top 3 customers on eu-prod-2; two are noticing heavy tail stalls, one is turning off streaming to retry. They're asking for ETA.
Marco (eng-runtime): Looking at runtime metrics — continuous batcher backlog + KV warmup queue growth. Autoscaler reports scale events but warmup handshake to new instances is taking longer than usual (~14-20s), causing in-flight requests to queue. Investigating root cause for warmup churn.
Sam (eng-ml): I can confirm model loading times spiked for the quantized weights on eu-prod-2. Memory pressure + cold KV cache increased model init. p95 model-init went from 200ms -> 5s, p99 -> 18s in the last 10m.
Alex (infra-oncall): I'm ready to manually add capacity. Would prefer to autoscale fix, but for immediate mitigation I can add 3 hotshot instances to the pool.
Nora (oncall): Do it. Also, we should enable model fallbacks to the smaller variant for streaming routes temporarily. Marco — can we route a subset of traffic to hosted fallback? :thumbsup:
Marco (eng-runtime): Yes — we have a compatible smaller model (m-small-v2). I can flip routing for the high-latency route to use m-small-v2 for 20% of traffic (canary) and increase if stable. Applying now.
Marco (eng-runtime): Applying rule: `route set /v1/stream/chat model=m-small-v2 percent=20 pool=eu-prod-2` — rolling out.
Sam (eng-ml): Enabling smaller model will lower quality slightly but should drop warmup time <1s. Recommend notifying CS.
Tara (cust-success): Notifying customers about temporary fallback and apology. Will mention we're prioritizing reliability.
Alex (infra-oncall): Manual scale command run: `rictl pool resize --pool eu-prod-2 --add-instances 3 --type hotshot` — instances provisioning. Also bump warmup concurrency to 6: `rictl warmup config --pool eu-prod-2 --concurrency 6`.
incident-bot: Deploy log: instance-provision-started (eu-prod-2) id=inst-az3 1765554330
Marco (eng-runtime): Observability: queue_depth metric peaked at 212, now trending down to ~120 after routing change. Streaming p99 improving from 34s -> ~18s within 90s. Continuing to monitor.
Blake (support): AcmeApp confirmed partial improvement after fallback, but still seeing occasional single-chunk stalls. They asked for estimated time to fully restore.
Marco (eng-runtime): Dumping recent warmup logs for new instances:
```
[1765554335] instance inst-az3 warmup: pulling model m-large-v3
[1765554341] model load start
[1765554347] kv-cache miss flood: 120k keys queued
[1765554359] model init complete (14.2s)
[1765554362] handshake complete
```
Sam (eng-ml): That kv-cache miss flood is suspicious — maybe cache evictions from other pools. I'll check cross-pool eviction heuristics.
Alex (infra-oncall): New instances are healthy and registered. Pool capacity +3 completed 1765554365.
Marco (eng-runtime): p95 now ~1.1s, p99 ~9.8s. Still above target but much better. Streaming stalls have dropped by ~70% per telemetry.
Nora (oncall): Good. Next steps: 1) keep manual +3 until autoscaler corrected; 2) Marco + Sam to debug warmup handshake length root cause; 3) Alex to confirm warmup config changes persist; 4) CS to update customers. Anyone want to add?
Priya (prod): Please capture impact window and affected customers for post-incident review. We'll need RCA and postmortem.
Tara (cust-success): Sending customer churn risk note for AcmeApp and BetaClient. Both had degraded experiences; AcmeApp applied fallback but might ask for credits.
Marco (eng-runtime): Preliminary hypothesis: autoscaler is healthy but new instance warmup blocked on KV cache coldpath due to concurrent mass restarts in eu-prod region around 10:12 UTC (some infra job triggered compaction). Sam/infra to confirm.
Sam (eng-ml): Found correlation: a GC compaction job ran on shared NFS at 10:10 which caused transient IO latency spikes and evicted many KV entries. We should pin KV store to local SSD for dedicated pools or adjust eviction policy.
Alex (infra-oncall): Will disable the non-critical compaction run for NFS in eu region and patch the job to respect pool tags. Doing now.
incident-bot: Action logged: manual-scale + fallback route applied + warmup concurrency bump. Severity: Sev2. Page closed? No, still monitoring. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
Blake (support): Customers notified. Will collect any further logs and escalate if they reopen.
Marco (eng-runtime): Monitoring window: leave this thread open for 30m. I'll post a short postmortem draft when we have root cause data. Current status: mitigated -> partial restore.
Nora (oncall): Thanks everyone. If p99 drops below 5s and no new customer reports in 30m we'll close. Otherwise escalate to Sev1. :white_check_mark:
Priya (prod): Assigning follow-ups: Marco (warmup root cause & fix), Sam (kv eviction memory policy), Alex (infra job change & autoscaler tuning), Tara (customer follow-ups). I'll create the postmortem ticket and link it.
Marco (eng-runtime): Quick note for postmortem: include the warmup timeline, kv-cache miss counts, instance init durations, and routing fallback decision timestamps.
incident-bot: Alert cleared from active-firing to mitigated at 1765554378.
